name: Little Girl and Problem on Trees
description: A little girl loves problems on trees very much. Here's one of them. A tree is an undirected connected graph, not containing cycles. The degree of node x in the tree is the number of nodes y of the tree, such that each of them is connected with node x by some edge of the tree. Let's consider a tree that consists of n nodes. We'll consider the tree's nodes indexed from 1 to n . The cosidered tree has the following property: each node except for node number 1 has the degree of at most 2. Initially, each node of the tree contains number 0. Your task is to quickly process the requests of two types: Request of form: 0 v x d . In reply to the request you should add x to all numbers that are written in the nodes that are located at the distance of at most d from node v . The distance between two nodes is the number of edges on the shortest path between them. Request of form: 1 v . In reply to the request you should print the current number that is written in node v .
input_specification: The first line contains integers n ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) and q ( 1 ≤ q ≤ 10 5 ) — the number of tree nodes and the number of requests, correspondingly. Each of the next n -  1 lines contains two integers u i and v i ( 1 ≤ u i , v i ≤ n , u i ≠ v i ), that show that there is an edge between nodes u i and v i . Each edge's description occurs in the input exactly once. It is guaranteed that the given graph is a tree that has the property that is described in the statement. Next q lines describe the requests. The request to add has the following format: 0 v x d ( 1 ≤ v ≤ n , 1 ≤ x ≤ 10 4 , 1 ≤ d < n ). The request to print the node value has the following format: 1 v ( 1 ≤ v ≤ n ). The numbers in the lines are separated by single spaces.
output_specification: For each request to print the node value print an integer — the reply to the request.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 276E — Little Girl and Problem on Trees [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
